answer.rationale: Incumbent has refused price reopen, but the contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so there is leverage on payment terms, volume tiers, and term length even if unit price is frozen. Memory c6 shows that multi-year commitments with the incumbent previously unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope — that lever is still available. I want to verify c6 to confirm the magnitude of unit-cost reduction and that service scope was genuinely preserved, since I am about to trade flexibility for price. I also want to verify c2 (low-cost vendor) because it is the realistic fallback / benchmark if negotiation fails: it establishes the floor on achievable unit cost and onboarding speed, which sets my walk-away point and confirms whether a switch remains viable within the 14-day window given 94% utilization with no buffer. I am not verifying c1, c3, c4, or c5 this cycle — c1 and c4 concern renewal posture without price pressure, c3 is a second-source tactic not addressable in one decision given capacity, and c5 (defer) conflicts with the hard 14-day expiry.
